s0201.literal: An edict said: "Rites for the end have their canon; these restrain the old statutes. Merit that may be weighed should rightly be honored from afar.
s0201.idiomatic: An edict said: "Rites for the dead have their canon and restrain the old statutes. Merit that can be weighed should rightly be honored from afar.

s0202.literal: Palace Attendant, Secure-the-Right General, Left Grand Master of the Glory, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Senior Rectifier of South Xuzhou, and Established Marquis of Jianchang county Ling—from youth his learning was lofty; on entering court he was outstanding; his accomplishment surpassed his generation and his writing made him patriarch of literature.
s0202.idiomatic: Palace attendant, secure-the-right general, left grand master of the glory, junior tutor of the heir apparent, senior rectifier of South Xuzhou, and established marquis of Jianchang county Ling—from youth his learning was lofty; in court he stood out; his achievement surpassed his peers and his writing made him patriarch of letters.

s0203.literal: We in recent years received him at the flowery court and drew him especially close. Though he often lay ill, We still looked for recovery; suddenly he fell and passed away, and shock and grief fill Our breast.
s0203.idiomatic: In recent years We received him at court and drew him especially close. Though he often lay ill, We still expected recovery; suddenly he died, and shock and grief fill Our breast.

s0204.literal: Let him be posthumously granted Secure-the-Right General and Special Advancement; his palace attendant, left grand master of the glory, musical guard, and marquisate remain as before; mourning is to be proclaimed throughout, and funeral needs generously supplied.
s0204.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted secure-the-right general and special advancement; his palace attendant, left grand master of the glory, musical guard, and marquisate remain as before; mourning is to be proclaimed throughout, and funeral needs generously supplied.

s0206.literal: Ling's capacity and deportment were deep and far-reaching; his bearing was admirable. His nature was pure and spare; he made no schemes for gain and shared his salary with kinsmen.
s0206.idiomatic: Ling's capacity and bearing were deep and admirable. His nature was pure and spare; he schemed for nothing and shared his salary with kin.

s0207.literal: In the Taijian era, while drawing income from Jianchang fief, district households brought grain to the riverside. Poor among his kin he had take it all; in a few days it was gone and his own household soon faced want.
s0207.idiomatic: In the Taijian era, while drawing income from Jianchang fief, district households brought grain to the riverside. He had poor kin take it all; in a few days it was gone and his own household soon faced want.

s0208.literal: His office colleagues wondered and asked why.
s0208.idiomatic: His office colleagues wondered and asked why.

s0209.literal: Ling said: "I have oxen, carts, and clothes to sell—do the rest of you lack things to sell?
s0209.idiomatic: Ling said, "I have oxen, carts, and clothes to sell—do the rest of you lack things to sell?

s0210.literal: " Such was his way of aiding others.
s0210.idiomatic: " Such was his way of aiding others.

s0211.literal: From youth he revered Buddhism and understood many sutras and treatises.
s0211.idiomatic: From youth he revered Buddhism and understood many sutras and treatises.

s0212.literal: When Houzhu was heir apparent he had Ling expound the Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra. Eminent monks of doctrine gathered from far off; whenever the lecture hall debated, none in the four seats could match him.
s0212.idiomatic: When Houzhu was heir apparent he had Ling expound the Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra. Eminent monks gathered from afar; whenever the lecture hall debated, none in the four seats could match him.

s0213.literal: His eyes had blue pupils; contemporaries took this as a mark of keen intelligence.
s0213.idiomatic: His eyes had blue pupils; contemporaries took this as a mark of keen intelligence.

s0214.literal: From Chen's founding, proclamations, military letters, and abdication investiture documents were all Ling's work, and his Nine Bestowals text was especially fine.
s0214.idiomatic: From Chen's founding, proclamations, military letters, and abdication investiture documents were all Ling's work, and his Nine Bestowals text was especially fine.

s0215.literal: Patriarch of literature for his age, he never lorded this over others and never reviled fellow authors.
s0215.idiomatic: Patriarch of letters for his age, he never lorded it over others and never reviled fellow authors.

s0216.literal: Toward rising men he showed tireless guidance.
s0216.idiomatic: Toward rising men he showed tireless guidance.

s0217.literal: In the reigns of Emperor Shizong and Emperor Xuan, whenever the state had a major literary commission, Ling drafted it.
s0217.idiomatic: In the reigns of Emperor Shizong and Emperor Xuan, whenever the state had a major literary commission, Ling drafted it.

s0218.literal: His writing greatly altered the old style: tightly woven and ingenious, often with fresh turns.
s0218.idiomatic: His writing greatly altered the old style—tightly woven and ingenious, often with fresh turns.

s0219.literal: Each piece, once issued, admirers copied and recited it; it spread through China and beyond, and households treasured his texts.
s0219.idiomatic: Each piece, once issued, admirers copied and recited it; it spread through China and beyond, and households treasured his texts.

s0220.literal: Later came disorder and ruin; most were lost; thirty scrolls survive.
s0220.idiomatic: Later came disorder and ruin; most were lost; thirty scrolls survive.

s0221.literal: He had four sons: Jian, Fen, Yi, and Bin.
s0221.idiomatic: He had four sons: Jian, Fen, Yi, and Bin.

s0222.literal: Jian also bore the name Zhong.
s0222.idiomatic: Jian also bore the name Zhong.

s0223.literal: [20] From youth upright, diligent in study with firm resolve; Zhou Hongzheng of Runan prized his character and gave him his daughter in marriage.
s0223.idiomatic: [20] From youth upright, diligent in study with firm resolve; Zhou Hongzheng of Runan prized his character and gave him his daughter in marriage.

s0224.literal: At the opening of Liang's Taiqing era he began service as acting aide in the Prince of Yuzhang's household.
s0224.idiomatic: At the opening of Liang's Taiqing era he began service as acting aide in the Prince of Yuzhang's household.

s0225.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion Ling was on mission to Wei and had not returned; Jian, then twenty-one, took the old and young to refuge at Jiangling. Emperor Yuan of Liang heard his name and summoned him as director in the ministry of the gold office.
s0225.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Ling was on mission to Wei and had not returned; Jian, then twenty-one, took the old and young to refuge at Jiangling. Emperor Yuan of Liang heard his name and summoned him as director in the ministry of the gold office.

s0226.literal: Once at a feast he was asked to compose verse; Emperor Yuan exclaimed in praise: "The Xu house again has a writer!"
s0226.idiomatic: Once at a feast he was asked to compose verse; Emperor Yuan exclaimed in praise, "The Xu house again has a writer!"

s0227.literal: When Jiangling fell he returned to the capital.
s0227.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he returned to the capital.

s0228.literal: In Yongding's opening he was made steward of the heir apparent, then moved to eastern garrison staff adviser.
s0228.idiomatic: In Yongding's opening he was made steward of the heir apparent, then moved to eastern garrison staff adviser.

s0229.literal: In Tianjia year 3 he was promoted to secretariat vice director.
s0229.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 3 he was promoted to secretariat vice director.

s0230.literal: At Taijian's opening Guangzhou inspector Ouyang He raised troops in rebellion; Emperor Xuan ordered Jian to bear credentials and convey the imperial will.
s0230.idiomatic: At Taijian's opening Guangzhou inspector Ouyang He raised troops in rebellion; Emperor Xuan ordered Jian to bear credentials and convey the imperial will.

s0231.literal: When He first received Jian he arrayed guards in full strength and spoke with no courtesy. Jian said: "The affair of Lü Jia is indeed far off—has the general alone not seen Zhou Di and Chen Baoying?
s0231.idiomatic: When He first received Jian he arrayed guards in full strength and spoke with no courtesy. Jian said, "The affair of Lü Jia is indeed far off—has the general alone not seen Zhou Di and Chen Baoying?

s0232.literal: To turn calamity into fortune is not yet too late."
s0232.idiomatic: To turn calamity into fortune is not yet too late."

s0233.literal: He fell silent and did not reply, fearing Jian would sap his followers' morale; he forbade entry to the city and lodged Jian at Guguan Monastery under guard; for many tens of days Jian could not return.
s0233.idiomatic: He fell silent and did not reply, fearing Jian would sap his followers' morale; he forbade entry to the city and lodged Jian at Guguan Monastery under guard; for many tens of days Jian could not return.

s0234.literal: He once came out to see Jian. Jian told him: "The general has already raised arms; Jian must return to report to Heaven's Son. Jian's life is in the general's hands, but the general's success or failure does not rest on Jian—pray do not detain me."
s0234.idiomatic: He once came out to see Jian. Jian told him, "The general has already raised arms; Jian must return to report to Heaven's Son. Jian's life is in the general's hands, but the general's success or failure does not rest on Jian—pray do not detain me."

s0235.literal: He then sent Jian back by a secret road at full speed.
s0235.idiomatic: He then sent Jian back by a secret road at full speed.

s0236.literal: Emperor Xuan then ordered Zhang Zhaoda to lead forces against He and, since Jian knew the situation, charged Jian to supervise Zhaoda's army.
s0236.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan then ordered Zhang Zhaoda to lead forces against He and, since Jian knew the situation, charged Jian to supervise Zhaoda's army.

s0237.literal: When He was pacified Emperor Xuan praised him, granted ten slaves and five hundred hu of grain, and made him staff adviser to the Prince of Poyang, pacify-the-north, with concurrent status as secretariat gentleman.
s0237.idiomatic: When He was pacified Emperor Xuan praised him, granted ten slaves and five hundred hu of grain, and made him staff adviser to the pacify-the-north Prince of Poyang with concurrent secretariat gentleman.

s0238.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to national university academician and director of the grand craftsmen office while keeping the rest as before.
s0238.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to national university academician and director of the grand craftsmen office while keeping the rest as before.

s0239.literal: Soon he was made yellow-gate vice director, then heir apparent's junior mentor, with added direct-communication regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrent left vice director of the masters of writing; he was dismissed for an official matter.
s0239.idiomatic: Soon he was made yellow-gate vice director, then heir apparent's junior mentor, with added direct-communication regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrent left vice director of the masters of writing; he was dismissed for an official matter.

s0240.literal: Soon he was recalled as extraordinary staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing in the central guard with concurrent secretariat gentleman.
s0240.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as extraordinary staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing in the central guard with concurrent secretariat gentleman.

s0241.literal: Again heir apparent's junior mentor, then steadfast-prestige general and left commandant of the heir's guard while keeping gentleman status.
s0241.idiomatic: Again heir apparent's junior mentor, then steadfast-prestige general and left commandant of the heir's guard while keeping gentleman status.

s0242.literal: When Houzhu took the throne he was given harmonious-submission general, chief clerk to the proclaim-grace Prince of Jinxi, with acting charge of Danyang commandery affairs.
s0242.idiomatic: When Houzhu took the throne he was given harmonious-submission general, chief clerk to the proclaim-grace Prince of Jinxi, with acting charge of Danyang commandery affairs.

s0243.literal: Soon he left office on his father's mourning.
s0243.idiomatic: Soon he left office on his father's mourning.

s0244.literal: Soon recalled as harmonious-submission general, he rose through posts to interior magistrate of Xunyang; his government was strict and clear and banditry subsided.
s0244.idiomatic: Soon recalled as harmonious-submission general, he rose through posts to interior magistrate of Xunyang; his government was strict and clear and banditry subsided.

s0245.literal: Promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, he inherited the marquisate of Jianchang and entered office as censor-in-chief.
s0245.idiomatic: Promoted to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, he inherited the marquisate of Jianchang and entered office as censor-in-chief.

s0246.literal: Jian was fair by nature and fawned on none; Jiang Zong, director of the masters of writing and weighty in his day, was also impeached by Jian—Houzhu trusted him deeply for it.
s0246.idiomatic: Jian was fair by nature and fawned on none; Jiang Zong, director of the masters of writing and weighty in his day, was also impeached by Jian—Houzhu trusted him deeply for it.

s0247.literal: He also commanded the right army.
s0247.idiomatic: He also commanded the right army.

s0249.literal: Fen from youth had his father's manner; at nine he wrote a Dream Rhapsody. When Ling saw it he told intimates: "I wrote young, yet did not match this."
s0249.idiomatic: Fen from youth had his father's manner; at nine he wrote a Dream Rhapsody. When Ling saw it he told intimates, "I wrote young, yet did not match this."

s0250.literal: On leaving the commoner's garb he was made secretary gentleman, then heir apparent's chamberlain.
s0250.idiomatic: On leaving the commoner's garb he was made secretary gentleman, then heir apparent's chamberlain.

s0251.literal: He rose to registrar to the Prince of Yuzhang and steward of the heir apparent.
s0251.idiomatic: He rose to registrar to the Prince of Yuzhang and steward of the heir apparent.

s0252.literal: Sent out as magistrate of Haiyan, he achieved notable governance.
s0252.idiomatic: Sent out as magistrate of Haiyan, he achieved notable governance.

s0253.literal: When his term ended he returned as steward of the heir apparent.
s0253.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned as steward of the heir apparent.

s0254.literal: Fen was filial and brotherly. When Ling once fell gravely ill, Fen burned incense, wept, knelt, and recited the Classic of Filial Piety without cease day and night for three days; Ling's illness suddenly lifted, and kin all said Fen's filial feeling had moved Heaven.
s0254.idiomatic: Fen was filial and brotherly. When Ling once fell gravely ill, Fen burned incense, wept, knelt, and recited the Classic of Filial Piety without cease day and night for three days; Ling's illness suddenly lifted, and kin all said Fen's filial feeling had moved Heaven.

s0255.literal: He died in Taijian year 2, aged twenty-two.
s0255.idiomatic: He died in Taijian year 2, aged twenty-two.

s0256.literal: Yi was keen and alert from youth; as a student of the Changes he ranked high and became secretary gentleman, then went out as magistrate of Wushang.
s0256.idiomatic: Yi was keen and alert from youth; as a student of the Changes he ranked high and became secretary gentleman, then went out as magistrate of Wushang.

s0257.literal: At Zhenming's opening he was promoted to palace gentleman of the masters of writing, soon with concurrent eastern-palace academician.
s0257.idiomatic: At Zhenming's opening he was promoted to palace gentleman of the masters of writing, soon with concurrent eastern-palace academician.

s0258.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui.
s0258.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui.

s0259.literal: In Kaihuang year 9 he retired to Zhe Mountain in Qiantang; Emperor Yang summoned him as academician and soon made him director in the works office.
s0259.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 9 he retired to Zhe Mountain in Qiantang; Emperor Yang summoned him as academician and soon made him director in the works office.

s0261.literal: Xiaoke was Ling's third younger brother.
s0261.idiomatic: Xiaoke was Ling's third younger brother.

s0262.literal: In youth he was a student of the Changes, eloquent, and able to discourse on Neo-Daoist principle.
s0262.idiomatic: In youth he was a student of the Changes, eloquent, and able to discourse on Neo-Daoist principle.

s0263.literal: Grown, he mastered the Five Classics, read widely in histories, and wrote well, yet his writing did not match his learning.
s0263.idiomatic: Grown, he mastered the Five Classics, read widely in histories, and wrote well, yet his writing did not match his learning.

s0264.literal: At Liang Taiqing's opening he began as academician of the imperial university.
s0264.idiomatic: At Liang Taiqing's opening he began as academician of the imperial university.

s0265.literal: Utterly filial, on his father's mourning he nearly could not bear the grief; toward his birth mother Lady Chen he fulfilled every duty of support.
s0265.idiomatic: Utterly filial, on his father's mourning he nearly could not bear the grief; toward his birth mother Lady Chen he fulfilled every duty of support.

s0266.literal: At Liang's end Hou Jing ravaged the realm; the capital knew great famine and eight or nine in ten starved.
s0266.idiomatic: At Liang's end Hou Jing ravaged the realm; the capital knew great famine and eight or nine in ten starved.

s0267.literal: Xiaoke supported his mother but gruel could not suffice. His wife was Lady Zang of Dongguan, daughter of the garrison general Zang Dun, very fair of face. Xiaoke told her: "Famine is such that support fails on every side. I wish to marry you to a rich man in hope that we may all be saved—what do you think?
s0267.idiomatic: Xiaoke supported his mother but gruel could not suffice. His wife was Lady Zang of Dongguan, daughter of the garrison general Zang Dun, very fair of face. Xiaoke told her, "Famine is such that support fails on every side. I wish to marry you to a rich man in hope that we may all be saved—what do you think?

s0269.literal: There was Kong Jingxing, a general under Hou Jing, rich in wealth. Xiaoke secretly had a go-between present his wish; Jingxing came with many attendants and forced the marriage. Lady Zang left in tears; all grain and silk gained went wholly to support his mother.
s0269.idiomatic: There was Kong Jingxing, a general under Hou Jing, rich in wealth. Xiaoke secretly had a go-between present his wish; Jingxing came with many attendants and forced the marriage. Lady Zang left in tears; all grain and silk gained went wholly to support his mother.

s0270.literal: Xiaoke also shaved his head as a monk, took the name Fazheng, and begged food to fill the need.
s0270.idiomatic: Xiaoke also shaved his head as a monk, took the name Fazheng, and begged food to fill the need.

s0271.literal: Lady Zang too cherished the old bond and often sent gifts in secret, so want never cut them off.
s0271.idiomatic: Lady Zang too cherished the old bond and often sent gifts in secret, so want never cut them off.

s0272.literal: Later Jingxing died in battle. Lady Zang watched for Xiaoke on the road; many days passed before she saw him. She said: "What passed before was no betrayal on my part. Now I am free—I should return to support your household."
s0272.idiomatic: Later Jingxing died in battle. Lady Zang watched for Xiaoke on the road; many days passed before she saw him. She said, "What passed before was no betrayal on my part. Now I am free—I should return to support your household."

s0273.literal: Xiaoke was silent and gave no answer.
s0273.idiomatic: Xiaoke was silent and gave no answer.

s0274.literal: He then returned to lay life and they became husband and wife again.
s0274.idiomatic: He then returned to lay life and they became husband and wife again.

s0275.literal: Later he traveled east and lived in Jiayi lane in Qiantang, debating Buddhist sutras with monks until he mastered the Three Treatises.
s0275.idiomatic: Later he traveled east and lived in Jiayi lane in Qiantang, debating Buddhist sutras with monks until he mastered the Three Treatises.

s0276.literal: Each day he lectured twice: mornings on Buddhist sutras, evenings on the Rites and Classics; clergy and laity studying under him numbered several hundred.
s0276.idiomatic: Each day he lectured twice: mornings on Buddhist sutras, evenings on the Rites and Classics; clergy and laity studying under him numbered several hundred.

s0277.literal: In Tianjia he was made magistrate of Shan—not to his liking; soon he resigned.
s0277.idiomatic: In Tianjia he was made magistrate of Shan—not to his liking; soon he resigned.

s0278.literal: In Taijian year 4 he was summoned as secretariat aide but did not accept; he took vegetable food and long fasting, kept the bodhisattva precepts, and day and night chanted the Lotus Sutra—Emperor Xuan greatly praised his conduct.
s0278.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4 he was summoned as secretariat aide but did not accept; he took vegetable food and long fasting, kept the bodhisattva precepts, and day and night chanted the Lotus Sutra—Emperor Xuan greatly praised his conduct.

s0279.literal: In year 6 he was made national university academician, promoted to direct-communication regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with concurrent rector of the national university, soon confirmed in the latter post.
s0279.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made national university academician, promoted to direct-communication regular attendant of the scattered cavalry with concurrent rector of the national university, soon confirmed in the latter post.

s0280.literal: Whenever Xiaoke attended banquets he ate nothing; when the feast ended the delicacies before him were diminished. Emperor Xuan secretly noted this and asked secretariat gentleman Guan Bin, who could not answer.
s0280.idiomatic: Whenever Xiaoke attended banquets he ate nothing; when the feast ended the delicacies before him were diminished. Emperor Xuan secretly noted this and asked secretariat gentleman Guan Bin, who could not answer.

s0281.literal: From then Bin watched him by intent and saw Xiaoke tuck fine fruit into his sash. At the time Bin did not grasp his meaning; later inquiry showed he brought them home for his mother.
s0281.idiomatic: From then Bin watched him by intent and saw Xiaoke tuck fine fruit into his sash. At the time Bin did not grasp his meaning; later inquiry showed he brought them home for his mother.

s0282.literal: Bin reported the fact; Emperor Xuan sighed long in praise and ordered that from then on at feasts Xiaoke's serving before him be all sent back to nourish his mother—contemporaries praised this.
s0282.idiomatic: Bin reported the fact; Emperor Xuan sighed long in praise and ordered that from then on at feasts Xiaoke's serving before him be all sent back to nourish his mother—contemporaries praised this.

s0283.literal: In the Zhide era the heir apparent entered school for the libation-offering sacrifice; all offices stood in attendance. Xiaoke opened the Classic of Filial Piety as topic; Houzhu ordered the heir to face north and bow in respect.
s0283.idiomatic: In the Zhide era the heir apparent entered school for the libation-offering sacrifice; all offices stood in attendance. Xiaoke opened the Classic of Filial Piety as topic; Houzhu ordered the heir to face north and bow in respect.

s0284.literal: Xiaoke was plain and fond of giving, so he could not escape hunger and cold. Houzhu ordered the Shitou ferry toll granted him; Xiaoke used it all for feasts and copying sutras, spending each sum as it came.
s0284.idiomatic: Xiaoke was plain and fond of giving, so he could not escape hunger and cold. Houzhu ordered the Shitou ferry toll granted him; Xiaoke used it all for feasts and copying sutras, spending each sum as it came.

s0285.literal: In year 2 he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and attended the eastern palace.
s0285.idiomatic: In year 2 he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and attended the eastern palace.

s0286.literal: When Chen fell he entered the passes by the usual rule.
s0286.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered the passes by the usual rule.

s0287.literal: His household stood bare; his birth mother fell ill and wanted polished rice for porridge—he could not always provide it.
s0287.idiomatic: His household stood bare; his birth mother fell ill and wanted polished rice for porridge—he could not always provide it.

s0288.literal: After his mother died Xiaoke ate barley regularly; when polished rice was sent as a gift he wept before it and never ate it again in his life.
s0288.idiomatic: After his mother died Xiaoke ate barley regularly; when polished rice was sent as a gift he wept before it and never ate it again in his life.

s0289.literal: In Kaihuang year 10 Chang'an suffered plague; Emperor Wen of Sui heard his fame and conduct and summoned him to expound the Diamond Prajna Sutra in the main hall of the masters of writing.
s0289.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 10 Chang'an suffered plague; Emperor Wen of Sui heard his fame and conduct and summoned him to expound the Diamond Prajna Sutra in the main hall of the masters of writing.

s0290.literal: Soon he was made national university academician.
s0290.idiomatic: Soon he was made national university academician.

s0291.literal: Later he attended the eastern palace lecturing on the Rites and Classics.
s0291.idiomatic: Later he attended the eastern palace lecturing on the Rites and Classics.

s0292.literal: In year 19 he died of illness, aged seventy-three.
s0292.idiomatic: In year 19 he died of illness, aged seventy-three.

s0293.literal: At the end he sat upright chanting the Buddha's name; a rare strange fragrance filled the room and neighbors were all astonished.
s0293.idiomatic: At the end he sat upright chanting the Buddha's name; a rare strange fragrance filled the room and neighbors were all astonished.

s0294.literal: His son Wanzai served up to clerk on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an and steward of the heir apparent.
s0294.idiomatic: His son Wanzai served up to clerk on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an and steward of the heir apparent.

s0295.literal: The historiographer says: Xu Xiaomu drew the finest of the five phases and received Heaven and Earth's spirit—keen intelligence that embraced past and present.
s0295.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Xu Xiaomu drew the finest of the five phases and received Heaven and Earth's spirit—keen intelligence that embraced past and present.

s0296.literal: When he helped frame the rising dynasty and met a great fortune, he rose to foremost minister and offered counsel in and out—plainly the upright heart remained.
s0296.idiomatic: When he helped frame the rising dynasty and met a great fortune, he rose to foremost minister and offered counsel in and out—plainly the upright heart remained.

s0297.literal: Xiaoke honed body and conduct and nurtured kin beyond the rites—is this not the resolve of Zeng Shen and Min Ziqian?
s0297.idiomatic: Xiaoke honed body and conduct and nurtured kin beyond the rites—is this not the resolve of Zeng Shen and Min Ziqian?

s0299.literal: [1] "In Liang Putong year 2 the Prince of Jin'an was made pacifying-west general and colonel pacifying the barbarians"—according to the Annals of Emperor Jianwen in the Book of Liang, the Prince of Jin'an Xiao Gang received those posts in Liang Wudi's Putong year 4.
s0299.idiomatic: On "In Liang Putong year 2 the Prince of Jin'an was made pacifying-west general and colonel pacifying the barbarians": according to the Annals of Emperor Jianwen in the Book of Liang, the Prince of Jin'an Xiao Gang received those posts in Liang Wudi's Putong year 4.
